questions: Did line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall from 1.1 and 1.05 toward 0.5 or below?
With the wider span, does the signal still reach about ±2 and do the outer sensors read zero on the centre line, or do they add noise?
Do the sensor weights [2,1,0,-1,-2] still give a stable turn with kp 4 and kd 0.5, or does the larger signal per unit of error now cause oscillation?
If line loss is now low but the s-bend still ends off track with max_error near 0.06, is a lookahead of y 0.04 the next test?

intent: Change one variable against iteration 1: widen the sensor span from ±0.024 m to ±0.032 m at an even 16 mm pitch, keeping sensor_size 0.016, y = 0.06, and all other fields unchanged. Expected result: line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom fall below about 0.5, the s-bend finish rate rises above 0.2, and the oval holds its current finish rate.
learning: Iteration 1 showed that the 16 mm footprint alone halves line loss on the oval but barely changes the bends, which points to span rather than footprint size. Next, check whether the wider span removes the bend line loss before testing lookahead or track width.
rationale: Iteration 1 (16 mm footprints) helped but did not fix the problem. The oval finish rate rose from 16/20 to 18/20 and line_loss fell from 0.95 to 0.45. The s-bend barely moved: line_loss is 1.1 (was 1.2), finish rate is 4/20, and off-track exits are 16/20. The slalom is still 0/20 with line_loss 1.05 (was 1.9). rms_error stays low on both (0.017 and 0.022), and max_error on the s-bend is 0.056, close to the 0.06 m limit. So the robot is still losing the tape at the edge of the five-sensor array rather than tracking poorly. R1's rule applies: line loss is still well above 0.5 with the 16 mm footprint, so widen the sensor span rather than the footprint or body. I will keep sensor_size at 0.016 and move the outer sensors from x = ±0.024 to ±0.032, with the inner sensors at ±0.016 and 0. This gives an even 16 mm pitch across a 0.064 m span, so a tape displaced to about ±0.035 m still falls under an outer sensor. I am not changing wheel_track, mass, body or lookahead yet, so the result is attributable to one variable. The body_width field has no effect below about 0.19 m, so it stays at 0.12. I expect line_loss_events on the s-bend and slalom to fall toward or below 0.5, with a higher s-bend finish rate. Note for the Integrator: the sensor weights [2,1,0,-1,-2] now sit on a wider span, so the signal per unit of lateral error is larger; they may need to re-tune kp.
